1074.body:
## What the failing case actually did

`test/agent-run-componentization.spec.ts` > `S2b` failed on `no console/page errors expected`. Its `trace.zip` has exactly **two** `research-package/preview` requests, both 404, and the two bodies are different:

| time (UTC) | body | cause |
|---|---|---|
| 21:51:21.978 | `{"error":"File not found"}` | an `ENOENT` mapped to 404 at `services/api/src/http/index.ts:4381` |
| 21:51:35.966 | `{"code":"EXPORT_PREVIEW_RESOURCE_DELETED"}` | the preview was aborted because the Project was deleted (`research-export-previews.ts:197-213`) |

The same `stack.log` (artifact `mocked-e2e-results-standard-journeys`) shows the wider pattern on a Session that no longer exists: `GET /api/sessions/<id>/runs`, `/agent-activity` and `/execution-blocks` answered 404 over and over, because the page stayed mounted and every poller kept asking. The preview poll alone accounts for 56 of the 404s in that run.

## What this changes

1. **The API answers a preview poll of a deleted scope with `200 { state: "deleted" }`.** The panel is only asking "how big is the export for the Session I am showing"; once that Project or Session is gone, there is nothing to preview, and a 4xx here is what the browser turns into a console error. A preview aborted by that same deletion answers the same way. A **download** of a package whose Project is gone keeps its 404: that request is a mistake worth reporting, a poll is not.
2. **The export dialog stops offering actions on a gone scope.** Its own 3-second poll receives the same answer; from then on the estimate and file list stay on screen as the pre-deletion snapshot while **both export buttons are disabled**, and the alert says so instead of claiming nothing is left to preview.

   (An earlier version of this PR also stopped a `ResearchPackagePreviewMonitor` on that answer. `main` deleted that component in `63f20d9e`, and my rebase had carried it back in as a new file; it is deleted again here. Re-mounting it would reverse that commit and is a maintainer decision, not part of this fix.)
3. **The agent-activity panel stops asking too.** On `Session not found` it keeps the message it already renders and clears its list, instead of re-reading `/agent-activity` every 2 seconds forever.

The client turns the `deleted` answer into an `ApiRequestError` carrying `EXPORT_PREVIEW_RESOURCE_DELETED` (`apps/web/src/api/plugins.ts`), so both callers recognise it without parsing text.

The journey assertion in `test/agent-run-componentization.spec.ts:443` is **not touched** - no skipped console errors, no scoping by session, no filtered stream.

## What this does not fix

The first 404 of that case is `File not found`, an `ENOENT` inside a preview of a **live** Project: it precedes the delete and comes from the generic `ENOENT ? 404` mapping, not from the deletion. This PR only converts such an error when the Project or Session is in fact gone. Naming the failing read is separate work, now tracked in **#1099**; it is not claimed here.

## Scope of the API change

Only the polling shape ends quietly. `GET /api/projects/{id}/research-package/preview?sessionId=…&defaults=1` — the request a mounted panel repeats every 3 s — answers `200 {"state":"deleted"}` once its Project or Session is gone, and so does a preview aborted by that same deletion. A one-shot preview read (`?level=…` without `defaults`) keeps its `404 EXPORT_PREVIEW_RESOURCE_DELETED`, because there the caller asked once and the answer is worth reporting, and a package download keeps its 404 as well.

`services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts` > `preview deletion ends the poll quietly while shutdown and the one-shot read keep their status` pins that split: poll `200 {"state":"deleted"}`, one-shot 404, `503` still 503 for both shapes. Without the route change the same case fails with `actual: 404, expected: 200`.

## Verification

- `apps/web`: `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean on this head.
- `apps/web/tests/ResearchPackageGonePolling.test.tsx`: **1/1** — the file keeps only the `AgentActivityPanel` case, because `main` deleted the preview monitor in `63f20d9e`.
- `apps/web/tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx`: 8/8 with the changed panel, including the existing "session miss does not stick" case.
- `services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts`: 20/20 on this head, including the poll-200 / one-shot-404 / 503 split.
- **Not measured locally:** the mocked journey. This machine has no working pnpm install for the API workspace (the shared tree sits at a different commit), so that half is CI-confirmed.

## Screenshots — both deleted-scope states, in the export dialog

Captured on **`e7065e89`**: the web app served from this head's own source, with the real API running from the same head against a fresh data directory. The sample Session and its 15 workspace files are real; the Project is deleted through `DELETE /api/projects/{id}`, so the dialog learns about it only from its own poll — the case this PR fixes. No network mocking: the two states differ only in *when* the deletion lands.

**State A — the dialog was open with a snapshot, then the Project was deleted.**
The same 4742.5 KiB estimate and 15 files stay on screen, and the sentence points at them *above*, with both export actions disabled.

**State B — the Project was already gone when the dialog was opened.**
No cached snapshot exists, so the estimate and both scope cards read `—` instead of "Calculating size…", and the sentence says there is no size any more rather than claiming a snapshot.

**zh-CN — A before / A after / B after**

![zh-CN A before: estimate 4742.5 KiB, both export actions live](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1074/docs/screenshots/1074/head-e7065e89/zh-A-before.png)
![zh-CN A after: 预计 4742.5 KiB kept, alert 该项目或会话已不存在；上方为删除前的大小，已不能导出。, 后台导出 and 立即导出 disabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1074/docs/screenshots/1074/head-e7065e89/zh-A-deleted.png)
![zh-CN B after: estimate and both cards read —, alert 该项目或会话已不存在，已无法再读取大小。](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1074/docs/screenshots/1074/head-e7065e89/zh-B-deleted.png)

**en — A before / A after / B after**

![en A before: Estimated 4742.5 KiB, both export actions live](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1074/docs/screenshots/1074/head-e7065e89/en-A-before.png)
![en A after: Estimated 4742.5 KiB kept, alert This Project or Session no longer exists. The last known sizes are shown above; exporting is disabled., Background export and Immediate export disabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1074/docs/screenshots/1074/head-e7065e89/en-A-deleted.png)
![en B after: estimate and both cards read —, alert This Project or Session no longer exists; there is no size to show any more.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1074/docs/screenshots/1074/head-e7065e89/en-B-deleted.png)

What the capture script printed, read from the DOM rather than from the images:

```
A  STRONGS=["必要导出","完整导出","预计 4742.5 KiB"]  ALERT="该项目或会话已不存在；上方为删除前的大小，已不能导出。"
   BUTTONS 后台导出=disabled 立即导出=disabled          ERRORS=[]
B  STRONGS=["必要导出","完整导出","—"]                ALERT="该项目或会话已不存在，已无法再读取大小。"
   BUTTONS 后台导出=disabled 立即导出=disabled          ERRORS=[]
en A  ALERT="This Project or Session no longer exists. The last known sizes are shown above; exporting is disabled."
en B  ALERT="This Project or Session no longer exists; there is no size to show any more."
```

One caveat, stated rather than hidden: after a deletion the **other** session-scoped pollers (`/runs`, `/agent-activity`) still answer 404 and raise the app's "Session not found" toast. That is outside this diff and is not what is claimed here — the preview poll this PR converts is answered `200 {"state":"deleted"}`, which is why the dialog stops.

Screenshots live on the `screenshots-1074` branch, not in the diff.

## Acting on the review of `f29c77f6` (F6)

The review's two points, both in `e7065e89`:

**The sentence now follows what is actually on screen, not `preview` alone.** `preview` is cleared when a file selection changes, while `necessarySize`/`completeSize` keep coming from `defaults` and survive the gone answer — so in that window the two scope cards showed "1.0 KiB" while the alert said there was no size. The sentence is chosen from `preview !== undefined || necessarySize !== undefined || completeSize !== undefined` (`ResearchPackageActions.tsx:225`), and a new case selects a file, leaves the custom preview unanswered, lands the gone answer, and asserts the sentence admits the sizes the cards still show.

**The evidence and the description are from this head.** The captures above are `e7065e89`, in both locales and both states; the alt texts and the F4 bullet below now quote the current wording, and this section is the F6 item.

## Acting on the review of `0e226467`

Two items came out of that review; both are in `82c9a75c`.

**The gone answer now belongs to the scope that asked for it** (the unresolved thread on `ResearchPackagePreviewMonitor.tsx:40`). The monitor stays mounted across a conversation switch, so a rejection from the previous scope that landed after the switch marked the *new* scope gone, both effects returned early, and its 3 s poll was never re-armed. Each request now captures its scope and compares it with the current one before setting `gone`. Pinned by a case that mounts on one conversation, switches while the request is in flight, then lets it answer `gone` and asserts the new scope still polls.

**A gone scope can no longer be exported** (F2, the `[Needs a person]` item). The dialog's own 3 s poll receives the same `deleted` answer; from that answer on, both export buttons are disabled. The last estimate and file list stay on screen as the pre-deletion snapshot rather than being cleared, which is the maintainer's decision: the dialog is only reachable while the scope exists, so this state comes from a concurrent deletion (another tab or another client), and a snapshot beside a disabled action reads better than an empty dialog. The paragraph above that described the preview as gone was wrong about this and is corrected.

Note on scope: `apps/desktop` is unaffected — its export dialog lost this option entirely in #1082.
## Acting on the review of `8eede370`

- **F5 (must-fix, rebase artifact):** the monitor `main` removed in `63f20d9e` is deleted again, and its three test cases went with it. The test file keeps only the `AgentActivityPanel` case, which covers a component `App.tsx` really mounts.
- **F4 (copy):** the alert describes the retained snapshot instead of denying it. Its wording was corrected again in F6 — en "…The last known sizes are shown above; exporting is disabled." / zh "该项目或会话已不存在；上方为删除前的大小，已不能导出。" — because the first version said "below" while rendering after the estimate.

Both threads are answered and resolved. `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` is clean; the kept agent-activity case and the dialog case both pass.

1076.author: yuanzhou75
1076.body:
Refs #1071 — the accounting half. The retry is not in this PR, and the reason is at the bottom.

## What this changes

`test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs` could only name a provider fault when the text carried a 5xx status or one of the gateway's routing keywords. A gateway that answers **200**, streams records and then dies leaves neither: the only evidence is `read ECONNRESET` / `other side closed`. Those three real cases (DRB-58, DRB-59, DRB-75 on run 42907916462) therefore stayed plain `FAIL`, and the run reported `provider faults 0` for a provider outage.

The classifier now names that class: `{ code: "provider-transport", status: null }`, from the words themselves plus the gateway naming itself (`181001` / `model call failed` / `openAI API` / `chat/completions`).

**Why it is checked before the product-report rule.** The failed case text is the run's own summary and contains `delivery_status=failed`, which the existing `PRODUCT_REPORT` rule uses to keep a quoted provider status on the product's side. Here the wrapper is the product restating a run that died on the transport, not evidence that the product mishandled a complete answer — so the exact transport words plus gateway context win over that wrapper. A delivery miss with no broken transport, and an assertion diff, still classify as the product's own.

Naming a fault still does not pass a case. The accounting keeps `PROVIDER_FAULT` separate from `passed`: a planned case that only faulted stays unverified, exactly as the module's own contract says.

## Verification

`node --test test/support/tagged/tests/provider-fault.test.mjs` — 4 cases, all pass:

- the exact `delivery_status=failed … run_error=[181001] model call failed … APIError: read ECONNRESET` text → `provider-transport`;
- the same words without the gateway naming itself → `null`;
- a delivery miss, an assertion diff and a `181001` failure with a product reason → `null`;
- 503 / `no available channel` unchanged, 401 / 429 still decisions, and two disagreeing texts still yield no fault.

The other self-tests under `test/support/tagged/tests/` fail on this Windows machine for environmental reasons (they spawn node/pytest wrappers and expect the Linux layout); that is not caused by this change and CI runs them on Linux.

## Why the retry is not here

The approved change was "one bounded retry, only when no tool result has been committed yet". Reading the transport, that condition is stricter than it sounds: `packages/model/src/client.ts:555` retries only **pre-stream** failures today — "Once the stream starts flowing, errors surface to the caller" — and the failing case had already forwarded **1208 SSE records** downstream. A retry after that point would replay an answer the client already received.

So a correct retry has to restart the request only while nothing has been handed downstream, which is a real change in `packages/model` (restart inside the reader until the first chunk is yielded) and needs a mock-SSE test that breaks the socket after `200` with zero and with several chunks. I would rather land that as its own change with that test than fold a half-safe retry into an accounting PR.

The harness's own one-shot early repeat is also kept off this class for
the same reason. `retryableProviderFaults` would otherwise re-run a whole
journey for a case that broke on the wire, which would count as the retry
this PR says it does not contain; it now skips `provider-transport` and
still repeats a `provider-server-error` fault as before. A transport break
still reads `PROVIDER_FAULT` in the accounting and keeps the run non-zero,
but the Nightly does not re-run it until the bounded restream lands.

**Maintainer decision recorded.** The user answered the two options on the issue card: add the bounded retry **and** classify a status-less transport break as `PROVIDER_FAULT`. The answer was exactly `加重试，且断流记 PROVIDER_FAULT`. That authorises this `provider-fault.mjs` change; the retry half is deliberately not in this PR (see below) and has its own follow-up.

1078.author: yuanzhou75
1078.body:
Fixes #1070.

Both real-E2E evolve journeys clicked send and then waited for a Run that was never asked for. An `/evolve-design` send does not leave on the composer's submit: it stores the draft and returns, and the **"confirm evolution settings"** dialog's own button is what sends it. The journeys never answered that dialog, so the message was never posted — the shard `stack.log` contains no `POST /api/sessions/<id>/messages` at all.

## This is the test that changed, not the product

The dialog is intended behaviour. I read both clients before picking a direction:

| client | where | what happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| web | `apps/web/src/App.tsx:3770-3781` | `submitMessage` calls `setEvolveSubmission(...)` and returns for any `/evolve-design` input; only the dialog's `onConfirm` reaches `sendComposerMessage({ algorithm, direction })` |
| desktop | `apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx:920-932` | `submit()` calls `setDirectionDraft(...)` and returns; only the dialog's `onSend` reaches `sendDraft` |

Two clients implementing the same gate independently, with a dialog that carries the algorithm choice, the checkpoint pace, a custom JSON scope, direction generation and the retry carry-over, is a designed interaction rather than an oversight. The journeys were written before it landed and were never taught to answer it.

## What changed

- **`test/helpers/journeys.ts`** — `isEvolveCommand()` and `confirmEvolveDirectionDialog(page)`: wait for the dialog by its accessible name, press its confirm button, wait for it to close. `sendUserMessage` calls it only for an evolve command, so every ordinary journey is untouched.
- **`test/helpers/desktop-evolve.ts`** — the same pair for the desktop dialog. It also answers the no-sandbox `--allow-direct` alert, in the same shape the srbench journey already used (`:299-305`), so a Windows host behaves as before. `sendMessage` calls it only for an evolve command.
- **`test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts`** — the local `send()` does the same, guarded by the prefix. That matters because the same `send` is called twice: once with the command, once replying to a design checkpoint with an ordinary sentence (`:117`), and that second call must not wait for a dialog that will not open.
- **`test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts`** — answers the dialog between pressing Enter (`:315`) and `waitForNewRun` (`:317`).

`test/journey-evolve-initialization.spec.ts` also contains `/evolve-design`, but it asserts the draft stays unsent and never submits — I read it and left it alone.

## Why two component tests

The journeys select the dialog by its accessible name and press it by its label. If either is renamed, the real-E2E case breaks again in exactly the same silent way (no request, a timeout, and a green-looking journey report). So the words are pinned where they can be checked cheaply:

- `apps/web/tests/Evolve.test.tsx` — the `DirectionDialog` confirm step renders 确认演进设置 and 开始演进, labelled by its heading.
- `apps/desktop/tests/evolve-ui.test.tsx` — the same for `EvolveCreateDialog` in `submission` mode, and the create step's own 开始设计 is absent there.

## Verification

- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean (real dependency tree installed for this snapshot, not the stale one from another checkout).
- The two new component tests pass: `apps/web/tests/Evolve.test.tsx` 28/28, `apps/desktop/tests/evolve-ui.test.tsx` 37/37 (both run with the platform tag relaxed for this host, and reported as such rather than as a CI-green run).
- **Mutation-checked, four ways:** renaming the confirm title or the confirm button to anything else turns the matching test red, in both clients. Restored, both are green.

**What I could not run:** `evolve-compression-real.spec.ts` and `desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts` are `@real @tier:l4 @sandbox:bubblewrap` and need Linux with bubblewrap, the full local stack and a real model. This host is Windows, so the honest statement is that the two journeys are verified by the **Nightly** run that owns them, not by me. What is verified here: the types compile, the selectors match the dialogs the specs now drive (asserted in the component tests), and the confirm step's control flow is the one the existing srbench case already used for the same alert.

1082.author: yuanzhou75
1082.body:
Fixes #1079.

The desktop export dialog offered **包含完整轨迹详情 / Include full trajectory details**. This client has no trajectory feature to detail, and ticking the box breaks the preview, so the export cannot be started at all until it is unticked. The option is removed.

## What the evidence shows

`apps/desktop/src` has no trajectory surface: the only hits are Mol*'s molecular-structure format (`molecular.ts:cifTrajectoryFormat`, `StructureViewer.tsx`'s `BuiltInTrajectoryFormat` / `parseTrajectory`), the `packagePreview(...)` URL builder, and the three places this PR removes. There is no trajectory viewer and no `/trajectory` request; the web client has both (`apps/web/src/api/client.ts:46-50`).

The failure mode from the issue, reproduced on `4bb737c2` with one session and only the query changing:

| request | result |
| --- | --- |
| `preview?level=necessary&includeFullTrajectory=0/1` | 200, 33,280 B |
| `preview?level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=0` | 200, 201,441 B |
| `preview?level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=1` | **404, empty body, ~2 s** |
| `preview?level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=1&includeFullMemoryGraph=1` | 404, empty body, ~2 s |
| `GET /api/sessions/{id}/trajectory` (same session) | 200, 1,434,283 B |
| `preview?level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=1` on an empty session | 200, 1,105 B |

**I am not claiming a root cause for that 404**, exactly as the issue says. 1086.author: yuanzhou75
1086.body:
Part of #1085 — two commits: the preview-warming OOM fix (browsing no longer triggers five preview builds) and the desktop-shell recovery.

## Root cause

`GET /api/sessions/:id` called `exportPreviews.watch(...)`, and `watch()` → `warm()` built **all five** preview profiles (necessary, complete, complete + full trajectory, complete + memory graph, complete + both). A plain session read therefore queued five full export builds, and the 3 s `tick()` repeated them for every watched session. Each profile materialises every message, run, run-stream event, workspace file, artifact version, provenance record and a memory-graph snapshot, so five builds per read pushed the API past the default 4 GB V8 old-space limit and killed it. The shell only watched the stack during startup, so once the UI was healthy a dead API left the window on a dead origin while the shell still held the single-instance lock — a white window whose every relaunch exits as "second instance".

## Change

**Backend (`services/api`)**

- **Reading a session no longer warms anything.** The `watch()` call in the `GET /api/sessions/:id` handler is removed.
- **The background warm preheats only the `necessary` profile.** The four `complete` variants (trajectory and memory-graph materialisations) are computed on demand when the export dialog issues its own `defaults` request.
- The export dialog's `defaults` request still returns all five profiles; caching and revision invalidation are unchanged.

**Desktop shell (`win_desktop`)**

- The shell now watches the owned stack's exit for the life of the window. On an unexpected exit it auto-restarts once (re-running the startup flow, which reloads the UI).
- If the auto-restart also fails — or the crash reproduces on boot — the shell surfaces the failure on the loading page and releases the single-instance lock, so a fresh launch takes over instead of exiting as "second instance".
- A stack that stays healthy for 60 s earns a fresh restart budget, so a later unrelated crash also gets one automatic restart.

## Tests

- `research-package-http.test.ts`: "viewing a conversation does not warm previews" — a session read performs **zero** memory-graph export builds, and the dialog's `defaults` request computes the five profiles it shows.
- `research-export-previews.test.ts`: new "background warming preheats only the necessary profile" case; the existing default/caching/serialization cases still pin five-on-demand.

## Verification

- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean for `research-export-previews.ts` and the two test files. The full `http/index.ts` type-check and the `win_desktop` type-check (needs the `electron` types) are CI's; the local verification tree lags main.
- The warm behaviour was exercised locally: `watch` + `tick` produce exactly one `necessary` calculation, and `defaults` produces five.

## Not in this PR

- **Bounded preview work.** Opening the export dialog still computes the four `complete` profiles in one `defaults` request — applying the `necessary` filter before materialising run streams (or computing the profiles lazily) is a separate change. This PR removes the warm-on-read trigger that crashed the reporter's install while browsing; the dialog-open request itself is unchanged.
- The explicit heap budget / `--max-old-space-size` and RSS reporting is tracked in #1063 (a need-person runtime contract), not here.

1087.author: zhaochen39
1087.body:
The nightly and standard journey gates exposed several independent reliability issues: a stale Research Package preview poll could issue a 404 after the dialog/session lifecycle changed; a model stream could terminate after hidden reasoning with a network error even though the turn was safely replayable; and transient bridge reads could fail without a bounded, safe retry. This change keeps retries scoped to operations that have not been dispatched and removes the stale UI poll while hardening the affected test and teardown paths.

## Changes

- Remove the app-wide Research Package preview monitor and delete its now-unreferenced component; the open export dialog retains its own refresh lifecycle.
- Retry at most once when a task model stream is classified as a network failure before any visible text or tool call is emitted. Hidden reasoning is emitted only from the first attempt, auxiliary requests are never retried, and visible partial turns are never replayed.
- Retry `read_artifact` only for pre-dispatch `ConnectError`/`PoolTimeout` failures. `ReadError`, `RemoteProtocolError`, HTTP 5xx responses, and non-read tools remain single-shot to avoid duplicate tool execution.
- Keep wire `retries` consistent with the merged `retryErrors` list.
- Fix API teardown ownership and harden local-token onboarding navigation around reload/hash behavior.
- Add focused gateway, bridge, and onboarding regression coverage.

## UI impact

No visual UI changes. This PR only removes the app-wide background Research Package preview poll. The export dialog keeps its existing preview refresh behavior, layout, styling, and controls.

Screenshot: N/A — the change is limited to the background request lifecycle and produces no before/after visual difference.

## Validation

- Before the final review fixes, model and API builds passed.
- API and web TypeScript checks, test TypeScript compilation, and gateway retry/no-replay smoke checks passed.
- `git diff --check` passed for the updated commit.
- Per request, the UT, ST, and E2E layers were not rerun locally after the final review fixes.

## E2E user journeys

NOT RUN locally after the final review fixes by request. Existing Linux evidence identified the targeted failures: the mocked standard-journeys run reported 87 passed and 1 failed, with S2b failing only on a 404 Research Package preview request; the research-3 run reported an HTTP 200 model stream with reasoning, no text, no tool calls, and a final network classification. CI should run the repository gates on this pull request.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: research runs, bridge artifact reads, and token onboarding avoid the targeted transient failures without replaying unsafe tool calls.
Compatibility and migration: none.

1089.author: HongyeZhou
1089.body:
## What changes

`start-stack.mjs` restored a lockfile an interrupted mirror sync had backed up **before** killing the `uv` child it was waiting on, and `killTree` only asks: on POSIX it sends SIGTERM and `uv` keeps writing until it is actually gone. So a Ctrl-C during `uv sync` could put the mirror-resolved versions back into `uv.lock` right after the restore — exactly the failure the bash twin's `trap` closes, and the one the #834 follow-up records for the `.mjs` path. The handlers also exited straight away, so nothing waited for the child at all.

- `shutdown(code)` awaits `stopChildren()` first: kill the tree, wait for each child to exit, escalate to SIGKILL after 5 s if one is wedged, and only then restore. Both handlers and the normal exit go through it.
- `process.on("exit")` keeps a synchronous fallback with the same order — kill, then restore — because nothing can be awaited there.
- `runStep` registers its build child in `children` and drops it again on exit, so a signal that lands mid-sync can stop `uv`. A step stopped by a shutdown never settles, so the startup sequence cannot run its remaining env checks against a half-torn-down tree and answer `1` before the interrupt answers `143`.
- No handler runs when the process is killed outright — the desktop shell stops the stack with `taskkill /T /F`, and power loss or the OOM killer behave the same. Entry now restores a leftover `uv.lock.stack-backup` before anything can sync again; its content is pristine by construction, and `win_desktop/src/stack.ts` says so at the `taskkill` site.

## Scope note

The packaging half of #897 §3 — the locale-trim hook hardening, `build-payload.sh`, the launcher comment, and the six stale `services/<member>/uv.lock` doc references — **landed in `1d547054`** from another author while this was open. This branch is rebased onto current `main` and now carries only the start-stack side; the earlier review threads on those packaging files are moot.

## Verification

On the rebased head `32eaf788`, linux/amd64:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node --test scripts/start-stack.test.mjs` | 2/2 PASS |
| `node --test scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs` | 6/7 PASS |
| `pnpm ci:l1` | 4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed |

The two new cases drive a real SIGTERM at the script: one interrupts a mirror sync (a fake `uv` that keeps writing until it is killed) and asserts the lockfile is pristine and the backup is intact; one starts from a leftover backup and asserts the next start restores it. The `start-stack-lock` test additionally pins the handler's kill-then-restore order.

Fixture note: `start-stack.test.mjs` runs its fake `uv`/`pnpm` shims from `os.tmpdir()`, so the suite needs an exec-capable temp directory — on a `noexec` `/tmp` the shims cannot be spawned and the run fails as a launcher timeout rather than a real assertion. Point `TMPDIR` at an exec mount there.`r`n`r`nThe one `start-stack-lock` failure is the mutation guard `"the same harness FAILS on the pre-fix body that restored only on the happy path"`, and it fails the same way with **unmodified `main` files** in this container: it strips the `.sh` twin's trap and expects the mirror's rewrite to survive the interrupt, but bash here exits before the fake mirror gets to rewrite, so the guard reports `PRISTINE`. It exercises the shell twin, not this change, and it is pre-existing in this environment rather than a regression here.

Not run locally: the Windows desktop path (`taskkill /T /F` on a real stack) and the Windows binary jobs — PR-profile CI skips the distribution jobs, so those only run in the merge queue.

Refs #897 — partial. Item §1 (real-machine Windows install/uninstall smoke) still needs a person and a physical machine, and §2 (first-run `.py` completeness manifest) is the open design question the issue records; neither is in this PR.

1093.author: qingkwl
1093.body:
Part of #897 — the P0 item the #834 review identified as the merge-blocking follow-up: any interruption of a mirror-mode `uv sync` in `scripts/start-stack.mjs` could leave `uv.lock` dirty with its backup already deleted — unrecoverable, and the next start froze the dirt as the "pristine" baseline.

## The defect (three parts, per the #897 discussion)

1. `runStep()` spawned `uv sync` without registering it in `children`
2. `cleanup()` restored the lockfile backup **before** killing the children, and `restoreActiveLockfile()` deletes the backup as part of the restore
3. The SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers `process.exit` immediately after `cleanup()`, never awaiting uv

So a SIGTERM delivered only to the launcher: restored + deleted the backup, exited, and the still-running uv rewrote `uv.lock` with mirror-resolved content → dirty lock, nothing to save it. The desktop's normal shutdown route (`taskkill /PID … /T /F` in `win_desktop/src/stack.ts`) never runs the handlers at all — half the fix exists for that path.

## Two complementary halves

**A (handlers run: POSIX SIGTERM / terminal Ctrl-C)**
- `runStep` registers every child (uv included) in `children`, removes it on exit
- `cleanup()` kills first, restores after; on POSIX it waits synchronously (bounded, SIGKILL escalation) for the children to die — the handler cannot await, and a mere SIGTERM delivery followed by `process.exit` would re-open the same rewrite window

**B (no handler ever runs: desktop `taskkill /T /F`, power loss, OOM)**
- a residual `uv.lock.stack-backup` at startup is healed back over `uv.lock` (with a log line) before the build block can freeze the dirt as the baseline — as discussed in #897, the "self-heal at startup" proposal alone is not enough; both halves are needed

**Also:** corrects the `stack.ts` stop() comment that claimed `taskkill /T` runs "each service's own cleanup" — `/F` is TerminateProcess; nothing runs, which is exactly why half B exists.

## Tests

`scripts/start-stack-interrupt-safety.test.mjs` (new, all-platform tags — no host skips):
- shape assertions pinning both halves (registration, kill-before-restore, heal-before-build-block)
- a behavioural run of the sliced-out heal helper against a dirty-lock + pristine-backup workspace
- mutation-verified: reverting half A, half B, or the cleanup ordering (each individually) turns the suite red

Existing `start-stack-lock.test.mjs` (6 tests) untouched and green — its static invariants (handler ordering, finally shape) still hold.

## P1 decision points (from the #897 bot analysis — for the owner)

This PR deliberately contains **only P0**. The remaining #897 items need decisions before code:

| Item | Decision needed |
| --- | --- |
| §2 first-run completeness guard | (a) subject: `.py` count vs `.pyc`; (b) behaviour: assemble hard-fail vs bootstrap named log; (c) manifest location (`version.json` has no runtime reader today) |
| §3.1 locale-trim hardening | remedy for the silent early-return: fail the build (matches `assemble-backend.mjs` `fail()` style) vs actually create the dir + copy 2 paks |
| §3.2 stale doc refs | 6 confirmed locations (docs zh/en, launcher comment, `build-payload.sh` ×3 — the last three are the issue's omission) — no decision needed, ready to go once P0 lands |

1094.author: qingkwl
1094.body:
Part of #897 §3 — the smaller hardening items. (#1093 carries the P0 lockfile fix; this PR is independent of it.)

## §3.1 Locale-trim hook hardening

The `afterPack` hook's early-return branch logged `"creating with en-US + zh-CN"` while creating nothing. If a packaging flow ever staged locales after the hook, the ~30 MB W4 win would be silently lost with a log claiming the opposite. Remedies applied (the failing style, per the #897 discussion):

| Change | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Missing `locales` dir → **build fails** (matches `assemble-backend.mjs`'s `fail()` style) | the hook's contract is to trim a dir electron-builder staged *before* it; anything else is a flow change it must hear about, not absorb |
| Post-trim verification, **regex-independent**: ≤3 `.pak` remaining AND `en-US.pak`+`zh-CN.pak` present | the review asked for exactly this shape; my first draft reused the `KEEP` regex and the mutation test caught it — a KEEP regression would have passed trim AND verification together |
| Header no longer claims "only en-US + zh-CN" | `zh-TW.pak` is kept deliberately as the fallback for zh-HK/zh-MO system locales; now documented |

When Bash reports a missing command, the model-facing Shell projection currently drops the Runner's diagnostic and its recovery advice. Preserve only diagnostic `code`, `command`, and `instruction` across synchronous results, managed completion, and execution management tools, while retaining the existing stream handling and credential exclusions.

Clarify that an unavailable managed Shell leaves the independent Python execution channel unaffected; `python -c` through `run_shell` still requires Bash. Extend native Windows command-shim coverage to both `.cmd` and `.bat`, literal metacharacters, and explicit rejection of unsupported characters.

Follow-up to #716; related to #916. The diagnostic projection regression was introduced after #716's original managed execution path.

## Validation

- Native Windows 11 x64 (10.0.26200), Node 22.23.4, local Runner, `none` execution mode.
- Diagnostic projection and Runner diagnostic tests: **8 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Before the product fix, all six affected projection entry points failed because the diagnostic was missing.
- Stack-platform/helper tests: **13 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Both shim extensions preserve spaces, `&`, and literal `%PATH%`; NUL, CR, LF, and quotes are explicitly rejected.
- Product build and test TypeScript check passed.
- Additional selected existing regressions: **12 executed, 11 passed, 1 environment failure**. The failure occurs while preparing a Windows symlink (`EPERM`), before Shell execution. These Linux-tagged tests were run from temporary copies with Windows added to the tags; assertions were unchanged. Initial platform-excluded runs are not counted as passes.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS:** Six chat scenarios through the running product's HTTP API and a local scripted model: immediate missing-command diagnosis, background completion observed through `execution_status`, stdout false-positive rejection, successful guaranteed utilities, pre-dispatch Shell refusal with no execution record, and successful Shell execution after restoring Bash. All six Runs completed and the model-facing tool messages were inspected.

Additional real Runner/setup acceptance:

- A fresh starter provides the six guaranteed utilities. `sort` also works, recorded only as an additional observation.
- A genuine old starter was created through product setup at `b31f74eb368a0e07848c2aa72acf9451348471bb`, whose Windows package contract adds only `m2-bash`. The candidate requests only `m2-coreutils`, `m2-grep`, and `m2-sed`, creates an audit revision, and preserves the original revision.
- Restarting after upgrade leaves the catalog and all **16,847 installed file hashes unchanged**, with no extra revision.
- With only the isolated instance's Bash unavailable, Runner readiness remains true, independent Python HTTP execution succeeds, and accepted managed Shell submissions settle as deterministic `not_started` failures without a fabricated result or version.

Setup/starter remain failed and scientific environment capability is unavailable; the original audit revision remains. Independent system Python still executes. 1096.body:
## What changes

`GET /health` and `/api/health` on the API, and `GET /health` on the Runner, answer ahead of the token gate on purpose — the container health checks have no token. They returned the Runner's whole record to everyone who could reach the port: platform, Runner version, execution user, sandbox egress allowlist, workspace quotas, scientific-environment and NPU capabilities. A default install binds `127.0.0.1`, but a deployment published with `SCIENCE_AGENT_PUBLISH_HOST=0.0.0.0`, or a Runner on another machine for remote execution, exposed exactly the reconnaissance an attacker of the sandbox wants first.

The routes stay public and the unauthenticated answer shrinks to liveness:

| route | without a valid token | with one |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API `GET /health`, `/api/health` | `{service, liveness}` | the full record as before |
| Runner `GET /health` | `{status}` | the full record as before |

A missing token and a wrong token both get liveness only, so the route no longer tells a caller whether it guessed a credential.

## Readers that follow the contract

- `RunnerClient.health()` sends its token. It is still the first call on a connection, so the clock offset is still learned from the same response before anything is signed; an older Runner that answers the detail regardless keeps working.
- The desktop self-check reads the detail through the client it already authenticates, and its tip says what the credential unlocks instead of presenting liveness as an incomplete stack.
- The Docker deployment-contract job generates a job-scoped token, forwards it as `SCIENCE_AGENT_AUTH_TOKEN` and uses it for the diagnostic read; the public liveness poll, and the Runner status/sandbox assertions, are unchanged.
- The shared real-E2E helpers and the desktop L3 suite (`apps/desktop/e2e-real/support.ts`, added after the first attempt at this change) send the configured token. That suite used to read `runner.status` off the public answer; it now reads it authenticated, and when a stack answers liveness only it tells a wrong credential (a failure) from a missing one (a skip) on an authenticated route.
- English and Chinese REST documentation states the public key set.

## Route shape

This keeps the detail on the same route with a token-dependent payload, which keeps the container checks token-free and needs no second URL. The alternative the issue left open — a separate authenticated route — would leave `/health` always liveness-only; say so in review if that is preferred and I will redo it that way instead. Merging this is the decision that the token-dependent shape is the owner.

## Desktop surface

The user-visible difference is one tooltip string and one dot state in the first-run self-check, plus the packaged wizard now reading the Runner through the authenticated route instead of the public one:

| where | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SetupWizard self-check, Runner row, English tip | `Not checked` | `Not checked (token required)` |
| same, Chinese tip | `未检查` | `未检查（需要令牌）` |
| SetupWizard self-check, Runner row dot when the browser probe gets an answer that carries a Runner which is not ready | green `✓` | `✗` |
| packaged first-run wizard (`win_desktop/src/wizard-api.ts`) Runner readiness | anonymous probe of the Runner port, `execution.ready` | `GET /api/health` with the token, `runner.execution.ready` |

No before/after screenshot is attached, and I would rather not attach a made-up one. The tip is the `<span class="boot-dot">` element's native `title`, so the page bitmap is identical before and after: the row is still a `–` glyph, and a browser screenshot cannot contain a native tooltip. The state that produces the new string is a skip, which by definition paints nothing else differently. Capturing it would need a real OS-level hover capture of a state that an isolated stack did not reach: without a credential the wizard stops on the credential screen, and with one the Runner row is checked and green (`selfCheckTip` is only reached for a skipped row).

What can be checked instead, on this head:

- `selfCheckTip(key, state, runnerNeedsToken)` is exported so the decision lives in one place, and `apps/desktop/tests/boot-screens.test.tsx` covers all three branches: a token-required Runner row yields `Not checked (token required)`, any other skip yields `Not checked`, a checked row yields no tooltip — 8/8 PASS.
- `win_desktop/test/wizard-api.test.ts` answers public liveness without a token and the full detail with one — 7/7 PASS; with the pre-change body restored, 3 of them fail.

## Verification

Recorded at `396ee89d`; the current head `234144cd` differs from it by two contract comments and one optional field declaration. linux/amd64, WSL-hosted build tree with bubblewrap available, and the API file compared against a clean worktree on the PR base `a773942a`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `services/api/src/server.test.ts` | 118 planned / 116 passed / 2 failed — the base is 116 / 114 / 2 with the same two cases |
| `node test/api/health-visibility-journey.mjs` | PASS, 4 steps, 0 failed |
| `apps/desktop` unit suites | 126 suites, 1137 tests, 1137 passed |
| `win_desktop` unit tests | 224 tests, 220 passed, 4 failed — the Linux-only cases below |
| `pnpm ci:l1` | 4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed |
| `pnpm build`, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`, `typecheck` (api, runner, executor, desktop) | PASS, PASS, 4/4 |
| `services/runner/src/server.test.ts` 54/56, `runner-client.test.ts` 7/7, `remote-compute.test.ts` 25/25, `sandbox-network.test.ts` 7/8 | failures reproduce on unmodified `main` or need real egress |

Neither api failure is this change's: `PDF upload extracts full text and tables into the session workspace` needs the `services/paper` environment this worktree does not have (`spawn …/services/paper/.venv/bin/python ENOENT`), and `API runs one observable subagent through task and keeps nested task denied` diffs `reasoningTokens: null` in the expectation against an object without that key. Both reproduce on the base. The four `win_desktop` failures are Linux-only platform cases (`bootstrapPackaged` twice, the repo-root default, `killStackTree`'s spawned pid); the file this branch touches, `wizard-api.test.ts`, is 7/7, and 3 of those fail with the pre-change body restored. The Runner's two long-socket-path egress cases and `sandbox-network`'s real-egress case need a container `main` does not have either.

The previous push's UT failure was mine: two reads in the managed-recovery test still took the Runner's health detail without a credential (the pre-submission capabilities check and the restarted server's identity), so they saw liveness only. Both now send the token, like every other health read in that file, and the unauthenticated route keeps its own case. The same head also rebases onto the merged #1044/#935 work, so `specialistErrorStatus` stays exported beside the health gate.

Production HTTP journey, `node test/api/health-visibility-journey.mjs` — **PASS, 4 steps, 0 failed**, recorded against this commit:

1. Isolated production API and Runner listening on ephemeral loopback ports.
2. Six unauthenticated responses (missing and wrong token, both API routes and the Runner) are HTTP 200 with exactly the public key set and no deployment detail.
3. Three authenticated responses keep their diagnostic fields, including the API's aggregation of the Runner.
4. With the Runner stopped, public liveness stays HTTP 200 and the authenticated diagnosis names the unavailable Runner.

Not run locally: the mocked and real browser E2E suites, and the Docker/binary/macOS startup paths. The desktop L3 change is typechecked but not executed — it needs a real stack and a real model. PR-profile CI skips the distribution jobs, so the deployment contract needs the merge-queue run.


## Self-check evidence (first run, desktop web UI)

Rendered from this head against a local stack (API + Runner + desktop dev server), Chinese and English, 1008x1000 pane and a 480x146 crop of the self-check list.

| State | Chinese | English |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runner row ready | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/zh-selfcheck.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/en-selfcheck.png) |
| Runner stopped | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/zh-fail-selfcheck.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/en-fail-selfcheck.png) |

Full panes: [zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/zh-pane.png), [en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/en-pane.png), [zh, Runner stopped](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/zh-fail-pane.png), [en, Runner stopped](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/267-selfcheck/docs/images/health-selfcheck/en-fail-pane.png).

The third state in the review — "token required" — has no capture because the shipped wizard cannot reach it:

- with no token, ^Gpps/desktop/src/App.tsx (the 	oken === "" branch) renders AuthScreen and the wizard never mounts;
- with a token the server refuses, the 401 on /api/settings runs onAuthRejected, which clears the token, so the app is back on AuthScreen before a self-check list exists.

health.runner === undefined therefore only happens in a version mismatch — a new app against an old API — and 
unnerNeedsToken is defence for that, not a state the UI can show today. The skipped row is captured on the model row instead: – with 	itle="未检查" / "Not checked".

Both skip reasons paint the same –; only the 	itle differs, and a native tooltip cannot appear in a bitmap. Those three tooltip cases are pinned in ^Gpps/desktop/tests/boot-screens.test.tsx (selfCheckTip: the token reason, a skip for any other reason, and no tooltip once a row was checked).

Not captured: the packaged Windows shell's wizard self-check rows (zh-CN and en, ready and not-ready) — a Windows build of the shell is not available here. The readiness source for that row changed (anonymous probe of the Runner port → `runner.execution.ready` read out of the authenticated `/api/health` detail), but the row's rendering and its two dot states are the same code path as the desktop wizard's, captured above; `win_desktop/test/wizard-api.test.ts` pins the two answers that drive them (7/7, and 3 of them fail with the pre-change body restored). The rows are therefore unchanged in every state I have seen, and what they paint now comes from the credential the wizard already holds.

Fixes #267

Closes #1091

## What was wrong

`DirectionInput` disables the generate button with `disabled={busy || !onGenerate}`, and the handler returns on its first line (`if (!onGenerate || busy) return;`), so a click dispatches no event at all. "Nothing happens: no loading, no toast, no error" is therefore the only possible outcome, not an intermittent one.

Two things made that read as a broken feature instead of an unavailable one:

1. **The disabled row looked enabled.** `.evolve-json-tools button` in `evolve.css` carried `cursor: pointer` and full contrast, and neither stylesheet had a `:disabled` rule for it (the web sheet has none at all). The same file already greys `.evolve-create-submit:disabled` and `.evolve-checkpoint-actions button:disabled`, so this was an omission rather than a style.
2. **The hint named the wrong reason.** `onGenerate` reaches the input only while the session has a loaded detail — `App.tsx:935` derives it from `state.detail` and `Composer.tsx:1217` passes it through — so its absence means "no session yet". The hint said "enter the task in the composer", which is why the reporter's natural next step (typing a task) could not fix it.

One correction to the report's own analysis: archived and read-only sessions do **not** remove `onGenerate` — `archived` only feeds `blocked`, which disables "Start evolution" — so no read-only branch is added; the only real reason is an unloaded session.

## Change

- `apps/desktop/src/styles/evolve.css`, `apps/web/src/styles/evolve.css`: add `.evolve-json-tools button:disabled` — with the footer and nested-row buttons, which `fieldset[disabled]` also greys while a generation runs — as `opacity: .55; cursor: not-allowed`, matching the disabled rows already in the file.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/evolve/DirectionInput.tsx`, `apps/web/src/evolve/DirectionInput.tsx`: replace the `needTask` copy with `needSession` — 会话尚未就绪：先在会话输入框发送一条消息，「生成起始字段」就会启用。 / "This session is not ready yet: send a message in the composer and Generate starting fields becomes available." The two files were byte-identical before this change and stay byte-identical.
- The enable condition (`busy || !onGenerate`) and the call path are unchanged: copy and styling only.
- On the web client the `needSession` line is unreachable today: `apps/web/src/App.tsx:5361` always passes `onGenerate`, so the web copy is kept in parity with the shared component and is not a live string there.

## Not in this PR

Making the action usable without a loaded session (create or reuse a session, then call `draftEvolveDirection`) is a behaviour change that reaches into the composer's send/session flow. The maintainer picked the smaller route on the issue; that route is not claimed here and would need its own change.

## Tests

`apps/desktop/tests/evolve-ui.test.tsx` — new case "the generate action names the real reason it is unavailable": with no `onGenerate` the button is still rendered but carries `disabled`, the hint names the session, and the old task wording is absent; with `onGenerate` the hint is gone and the button is enabled.

## Screenshots

The capture is the **real component** (`DirectionInput` rendered through `react-dom/server`) on the **real desktop stylesheet** (`apps/desktop/src/styles/index.css`, served over HTTP from a checkout at this head), both locales, each state side by side. It is not an Electron window: the change is renderer-level — a button's disabled styling and one sentence — so there is no native chrome to show.

![Generate starting fields: disabled with the session hint, and enabled once the session is ready, in zh-CN and en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1091/docs/screenshots/1091/generate-starting-fields-disabled.png)

A (no `onGenerate`): the button fades and the line below says the session is not ready. B (`onGenerate` supplied): the button is normal and the line is gone.

## Verification

- `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean, run against the exact files this PR pushes.
- `apps/desktop/tests/evolve-ui.test.tsx` declares `os:linux`, so the tagged collector makes it a no-op on this Windows host. I ran the same file with the platform forced to the declared one: 37/37 pass, including the new case. CI runs it natively.
- `apps/web`: the component change is the byte-identical file plus one added CSS rule, so there is nothing new to type-check beyond what the desktop package already checks. A full `apps/web` type-check is not usable as evidence from my checkout — it reports the same 17 pre-existing errors, in files this PR does not touch, with and without the change. CI is authoritative for that package.

## What changes

The run timeline's "N papers returned" line and the persisted tool trace each carried their own list of three source names (`arxiv`, `pubmed`, `europe-pmc`). bioRxiv and medRxiv return records in exactly the same gateway envelope (`sourceId`, `toolId: "search_preprints"`, `records`) and are already registered as paper producers, but neither site recognised them: a 25-record preprint search showed a truncated text preview and was indistinguishable from a search that returned nothing countable.

Both sites now take the answer from the **tool graph registry** — is `mcp__<sourceId>__<toolId>` registered with `product: "paper"` — through one shared helper in `@sciencediscovery/schema`:

- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` — `completedToolEvidence`, the persisted trace.
- `apps/web/src/timeline/research-label.ts` — `returnedPaperCount`, the tool card and group summary (plus `Orchestration.tsx` for the subagent step).

No name list is extended: the registry is already the single source of truth for what a tool produces, and it lists `mcp__biorxiv__search_preprints` and `mcp__medrxiv__search_preprints` beside the three older sources. A newly registered literature tool counts with no edit here, and registered non-literature tools (`uniprot` search, `pdb` search_structures) plus a non-search tool (`biorxiv` read) stay uncounted. Existing behaviour is preserved: provider `total` estimates and non-array `records` still yield no count, and 0 records still counts 0.

## Scope

Only the two count sites change. The **desktop frontend never renders that line and never reads `paperCount`** — the consumers are the old web timeline (`RunTimeline.tsx`, `Orchestration.tsx`) and the trace the API persists. I did not touch the frozen `apps/web` UI beyond the count function.
